title: It’s election day in Quebec: What you need to know to vote
summary: It's Oct. 5, which means Quebecers are heading to the polls today to shape the province's political future and determine who will lead the next government.

image.caption: Voting day in the Quebec 2026 provincial election is upon us. (Gabriel Claveau/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Montreal
It's Oct. 5, which means Quebecers are heading to the polls today to shape the province's political future and determine who will lead the next government.
Polling stations open Monday at 9:30 a.m. and close at 8 p.m.
It's Oct. 5, which means Quebecers are heading to the polls today to determine who will lead the next government.

Polling stations will be open on Monday from 9:30 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET. Your employer is supposed to give you at least four consecutive hours to vote on election day, with no reduction in pay or other penalty.

Voters should have received information by mail on where to vote, including a reminder card that was mailed in both official languages, following a provincial judge's order. The back of the reminder card also features the names of the candidates running in your riding.
You can also find your polling station by entering your address on Élections Québec's website.
As part of Élections Québec's aim to make it easier for people to get to the polls, the BIXI and àVélo bike-sharing services are offering free rides across the province from 8 a.m. to 8:30 p.m. ET.
Here’s what to expect as an anglophone when casting your ballot in Quebec’s election
If you're still unsure of who to vote for, the following tools have been designed to help prospective voters:

items: Vote Compass: developed by political scientists to help voters see how their views compare to parties and candidates.
Platform Tracker: compares the promises of Quebec’s five major parties.

blocks.text: The last two general elections have seen about two-thirds voter turnout, with approximately 66 per cent of eligible voters casting ballots (66.15 per cent in 2022, and 66.45 per cent in 2018).
Ahead of this election day, just over a quarter (25.59 per cent) of electors voted at advance polls between Sept. 25 and Oct. 1.
Election night coverage
CBC's live coverage of the election will begin Monday evening at 7:30 p.m. ET, and will continue until it's clear who will form Quebec's next provincial government.

The coverage will be available on CBC TV, CBC News Network and CBC Radio One. It will also be streamed on CBC Gem, CBC Listen, cbc.ca/quebec, YouTube and the CBC Quebec News streaming channel. ASL interpretation will be provided on the stream.

Viewers will be given up-to-the minute results and expert analysis from host Debra Arbec, chief political correspondent Rosemary Barton and political panelists Emilie Nicolas, Rodolphe Husny and Robert Libman. Sudha Krishnan and Douglas Gelevan will also break down the results, and live reports will come in from communities across the province.
CBC Montreal News at 6 will air at its regular time at 6 p.m. ET.
Post-election analysis

On Tuesday, Oct. 6, CBC will air a provincewide morning show election special on Daybreak Montreal. Host Sean Henry will be joined live by Quebec AM’s Gordon Lambie and Rachel Watts to provide analysis and reactions from across the province.

You'll be able to find it on CBC Radio One, CBC Listen or on the CBC News app starting at 6 a.m. ET (5:30 a.m. ET in Montreal). Beginning at 6:10 a.m. ET you can also watch on our website, CBC Gem, YouTube or the CBC Quebec News streaming channel.
